statement: The Jacobian J of C:y²+y=x⁵ has conductor3125 and CM by Q(zeta5), becomes a Hilbert modular abelian surface of level(sqrt5)³ over F=Q(sqrt5), and satisfies L(J/F,s)=L(J/Q,s)². Nonvanishing at1 implies finite J(F) and finiteSha(J/F) by the precisely stated Hilbert modular rank-zero theorem.
depends_on: Darmon2000 p439; Zhang2010 Theorem4.3.2 p588; CM induction and Artin formalism
answers: B.2 quintic arithmetic input; D exact theorem hypotheses and provenance
notes: The conductor exponent3 and trivial central character exclude a principal-series local factor. The published theorem is used as Known; its reference to Tian–Zhang is printed in preparation. No claim to have opened that unpublished work or the full inaccessible Nekovar PDF. The older Zhang2001 exponent-one theorem alone is insufficient.

statement: The root number of Jac(y²+y=x⁵)/Q is +1 and L(J/Q,1) lies in the certified ball 0.71831362842056477051660347805 ± 2.72e−30.
depends_on: A.50 CM analytic continuation and functional equation; exact finite-field Euler factors; Mellin inversion; explicit Bessel K bound; Arb outward rounding
answers: B.2 quintic finite-descent target; D certified L-value requirement
notes: 4096 exact Dirichlet coefficients independently expanded from every Euler factor and checked against lfunan. The root sign follows from the certified positive inverse Mellin theta value, not a database or numerical guess. Both infinite tails have elementary incomplete-gamma bounds below2.1e−30.

statement: Every Selmer section of the geometrically maximal prosolvable arithmetic fundamental group of the plus U5 is cuspidal.
depends_on: A.50 Known Hilbert modular rank-zero input; A.51; Stoll2007 section6; B.1 prosolvable finite-support theorem
answers: B.2 quintic maximal-prosolvable decision; Lead1 quotient scope
notes: Finite J(F) and finiteSha descend to Q by restriction and finite H1(Gal(F/Q),J(F)). Good reductions3,11 show J(Q)=C5; genus2 linear systems give C(Q)={infinity,(0,0),(0,-1)}. For the plus Fermat model x=-XY/Z²,y=X⁵/Z⁵, their complete fibre is the coordinate-cusp divisor. The conclusion is explicitly about the prosolvable quotient; no full-profinite lift is assumed.

statement: The entire plus Fermat quintic Jacobian is Q-isogenous to three copies of Jac(y²+y=x⁵), and therefore has finite rational Mordell–Weil group and finite Tate–Shafarevich group.
depends_on: A.50–A.52; three explicit cyclic quotient maps; plane-curve adjunction; isogeny invariance of rank and finiteSha
answers: B.3 quintic first-derived rigidity input; B.2 quintic maximal-prosolvable theorem
notes: The six pulled-back regular differentials have coefficients1,-XY,X²,-Y,Y²,-X relative to dX/Y⁴; their coefficient determinant in the six plane-quintic monomial basis is1. Every map and differential identity was verified exactly modulo X⁵+Y⁵+1. The least positive derived-length conclusion is proved separately in B.26; determinant1 is not an isogeny-degree assertion.

statement: Both Jac(y²+y=x⁵)(Q5) and Jac(X5)(Q5) have no prime-to-five torsion and are pro-five groups; their full local five-adic Tate Kummer maps are injective. The explicit isogeny and its transpose have kernels killed by five.
depends_on: A.50 exact CM conductor lambda²; A.53; local reciprocity; integral cyclotomic-polynomial identity; explicit trace characters
answers: B.3 quintic abelian rigidity; R9 geometric status of unramified-outside-five pro-five families
notes: A generator of the wild quotient U1/U2 has primitive fifth-root eigenvalues in every CM component. Phi5(tau)=0 and Phi5(1)=5 make tau−1 invertible on every stable Z_l Tate lattice for l≠5, including l=2. The same identity transfers by the rational isogeny without a degree assumption. A separate exact trace calculation gives PhiPsi=PsiPhi=[5]. No rank or finite-Sha input enters this local assertion.
